questions.answer_text: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form water, allowing electron flow through the aerobic electron transport chain to continue normally.
questions.explanation: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor. It accepts electrons and protons to form water, and this final acceptance allows electron flow through the aerobic electron transport chain to continue normally.

questions.answer_text: Fermentation preserves glycolysis by regenerating NAD+; it uses no oxygen as a terminal electron acceptor and produces much less ATP per glucose than aerobic respiration.
questions.explanation: Fermentation does not replace glycolysis. It regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis can keep running, uses no oxygen as a terminal electron acceptor, and produces much less ATP per glucose than aerobic respiration.
